Hi,

how it will help me in my analysis.

Did I understand correctly, that the interpreter will only work with
pure R code?
Many bioconductor packages rely on Fortran and C functions. So these
will not work?

Do you have examples for how interop Java <=> R will look like in the
end?

best,
ido

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: cool project
parts:
Hi Ido,

That's correct; C and Fortran code in such packages would need to be
either:
1. Ported to pure R
2. Ported to java
3. Compiled to JVM byte code via c2j or f2j or other similar project
(though some adaptation of C/F sources would probably still be
necessary)

These contraints mean that Renjin will not immediately be useful to
all current users; indeed the project is very much a work in progress;
using Renjin today means being will to get under the hood and tinker!
I hope the package maintainers might one day be motivated to provide
pure R implementations for their packages, but this probably won't be
tomorrow.

For R calling Java, I've started some preliminary docs:
http://code.google.com/p/renjin/wiki/JavaFromRenjin

And from Java to R:
http://code.google.com/p/renjin/wiki/CallingRFromJava

Best,

Alex
